arcs.title: Computation & reasoning
arcs.description: Build the execution, abstraction, proof, and cost models that every later system depends on.

arcs.title: Data & algorithms
arcs.description: Connect representation choices to operations, invariants, performance, and algorithmic strategy.

arcs.title: Durable software
arcs.description: Turn local reasoning into stable APIs, evidence, maintainable architecture, delivery, and transactions.

arcs.title: Machine & network
arcs.description: Modules 17–20 connect machine execution and OS mediation to explicit concurrent histories, synchronization, progress, deterministic reduction, and evidence-aware network protocols.

modules.title: Values, State, and Execution
modules.summary: Advanced Python, algorithms, databases, concurrency, and distributed systems all depend on one idea: a program transforms state according to rules. Bugs multiply when “variable,” “value,” “object,” and “memory” are treated as synonyms.

modules.title: Functions, Recursion, and Induction
modules.summary: Central idea: a function gives a computation a boundary; recursion gives repeated structure an executable form; induction gives the same structure a correctness argument.

modules.title: Abstraction, Interfaces, and Abstract Data Types
modules.summary: Central question: How can a client depend on what a component means without depending on how that component stores its data? Atlas transformation: a list owned by application code becomes a replaceable event store with one behavioral con…

modules.title: Logic, Sets, Relations, Graphs, and Proof

modules.title: Cost Models and Algorithm Analysis
modules.summary: Module 4 gave Atlas a precise prerequisite model and a correctness condition. Correct output is necessary, but it is not sufficient. A route validator that works for 20 concepts may become unusable for 200,000 concepts.

modules.title: Representation, Memory, Sequences, and Linked Structures
modules.summary: Central idea: an abstract history says what order means; a representation decides where references live, which paths connect them, and what each operation costs.

modules.title: Stacks, Queues, Iteration, and Lazy Computation
modules.summary: Central idea: constrain how stored work may be accessed, then let demand—not accumulation—control when work is performed.

modules.title: Hashing, Dictionaries, Sets, and Indexing
modules.summary: Atlas can now represent sequences, streams, contracts, graphs, and cost models. It still has a practical problem: a learner types hash collision, and Atlas must find matching notes without rereading every note.

modules.title: Trees, Heaps, Sorting, and Ordered Search
modules.summary: Central idea: a hash index answers “which item has this exact identity?”; ordered structures answer “what comes first, next, nearest, or under this prefix?”

modules.title: Graph Algorithms and Network Models

modules.title: Algorithm Design Paradigms: Choosing a Strategy from Structure
modules.summary: Central idea: an algorithmic strategy is justified by a structural fact about the problem, not by resemblance to a familiar code template.

modules.title: Modules, APIs, Types, and Dependency Direction
modules.summary: Central idea: a component boundary is a controlled promise about what may be known, called, and changed; Python modules and type annotations help express that boundary, but architecture determines whether it remains changeable.

modules.title: Specifications, Testing, Debugging, and Observability
modules.summary: Central idea: ambiguity becomes a specification; a specification creates testable claims; finite evidence localizes failures; observability preserves the missing context; each confirmed defect becomes regression knowledge.

modules.title: Software Design and Change
modules.summary: Arc III: Durable Software — pressure → contract → design → change → evidence A design is not “good” in the abstract. It is useful when it puts a likely change behind a boundary, keeps an invariant with its owner, and lets a reviewer tell…

modules.title: Files, Serialization, Packaging, and Delivery
modules.summary: Central idea: crossing a boundary turns implicit process state into an explicit artifact; that artifact deserves a representation, schema, compatibility policy, trust model, failure model, and evidence record.

modules.title: Relational Data and Transactions
modules.summary: Arc III: durable software — from a validated portable bundle to shared, constrained, transactional state A database is not “a faster file.” It is a system for representing relationships, enforcing invariants, coordinating operations, sel…

modules.title: Computer Architecture and the Execution Stack
modules.summary: Arc IV: machine, operating system, and network — from durable Atlas values to bounded explanations of how work becomes state change A Python operation is not a single machine action. It is a semantic request realized through several cont…

modules.title: Operating Systems and Resource Mediation
modules.summary: Arc IV: make the system legible — from an OS handoff to a supervised, recoverable Atlas worker An operating system does not make finite resources or failure disappear. It gives programs controlled abstractions for using them.

modules.title: Concurrency and Parallelism
modules.summary: Arc IV: make overlapping work explainable One worker can be correct in isolation while two workers, each doing locally valid work, produce a globally invalid result. Concurrency begins at that seam.

modules.title: Networks and Application Protocols
modules.summary: Arc IV: carry a local result across an uncertain boundary A local program can know that it produced a valid value. The moment that value must cross a network, it must stop pretending that one local event is a remote fact.
